bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds utilized for growth capital and acquisition provisions; No debt planned for next 2 years; Equity dilution/rights issue not anticipated in near term; M&A strategy focused on tuck-in acquisitions (like Edward Farr) at ~2.5x EBITDA multiples.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Receivable days expanded to 108 days (mostly related party, being cleared); Dependence on US market (80% of order book); Potential commoditization of low-end modeling via AI; Execution risk in integrating multiple US acquisitions; Seasonality (Q2 typically slower).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident and ambitious; Emphasis on 'transformational' year and global scalability; Transparent about upfront cost investments for future gains; Aggressive on growth guidance (60-70% CAGR) but conservative on debt.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Subsidiaries have zero attrition vs 10% in India; 60-70% of revenue is recurring from existing clients despite project-based nature; Management considers acquired subsidiaries' growth as 'organic' going forward since execution is fully integrated in India; Q4 strength driven by US decision-making cycles.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Global delivery model with integrated operations across India and the United States, enabling seamless project execution and client support
- 24-hour project execution capability from time-zone advantage, supporting faster turnaround
- Multi-disciplinary engineering expertise — Structural Engineering, BIM, Precast Engineering, Architecture and Project Coordination delivered under one platform
- Integrated service delivery combining BIM, Structural Engineering and Architectural capabilities for end-to-end project support
- Switching-cost / relationship moat: a significant portion of business is generated from repeat clients, supported by quality, execution accuracy and timely delivery
- Technology-first culture with continuous investment in digital tools, automation and BIM technologies
- Dedicated in-house R&D team driving automation and BIM technology advancement
- Engineering workforce skilled on leading platforms including Tekla, SDS2 and Revit
- ISO 9001:2015 certification supporting consistent quality and compliance
- Industry recognition including Trimble's Feature Company of the Month (2024) and panelist at Tekla User Day (2025)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Client concentration and order continuity — The Company derives a significant portion of its business from repeat customers, so any slowdown in client spending, delay in project execution, or loss of key customers may impact revenues and profitability. Mitigation is on-boarding new clients across geographies and engaging larger customers with better project visibility and higher ticket sizes.
- Geographic concentration in the United States and dependence on export markets — A significant portion of business comes from international markets, particularly the United States; management separately flags dependence on export markets such as the USA, UK and Australia among its key threats. Any slowdown in construction activity in these markets flows straight through to revenue. Mitigation is regional diversification into Canada, New Zealand and Southeast Asia.
- Talent availability and employee retention — The engineering and BIM industry is highly dependent on skilled manpower; inability to attract, train and retain qualified professionals may affect execution capability and service quality. Management also flags high dependence on skilled BIM professionals and rising employee costs as threats — a direct margin risk for a people-cost-led services model. Mitigation is continuous investment in manpower, training and R&D, plus multi-location delivery centres and structured training programmes.
- Technology and cybersecurity risk — Increasing dependence on digital engineering platforms and software tools exposes the business to cybersecurity threats, system disruptions and data security risks — material given the Company handles client design and project data across borders. Mitigation is strengthening IT infrastructure, project management systems and quality-control processes.
- Technology obsolescence from fast-changing software platforms — Management lists fast-changing software platforms among its key threats. The delivery model is built on specific engineering platforms (Tekla, SDS2, Revit), so platform shifts or new AI-driven toolchains require continuous reskilling and tooling investment to stay competitive.
- Foreign exchange risk — The Company is exposed to foreign currency risk on revenue from overseas contracts and on expenses and payments denominated in foreign currencies. Exposure is managed through natural hedging and ongoing monitoring; management states it does not foresee any material adverse impact from foreign exchange fluctuations. Management separately lists foreign exchange volatility among its threats.
- Competitive, technology-led industry with high client implementation cost and delayed digital adoption — Management flags that it operates in a competitive and technology-led industry, with high BIM implementation costs for clients and the possibility of delayed digital adoption. Slower-than-expected BIM uptake would blunt the primary demand driver the Company's growth thesis rests on.
- Execution and integration risk from an acquisition-led growth strategy — Growth depends materially on strategic acquisitions — four US entities acquired between December 2023 and March 2026, the latest taking the Company into a new service line (architecture). The Company itself states it must maintain operational integration and value creation, and its Board's Report emphasises alignment of a multi-geography, multi-entity structure; integration failure or overpayment would impair the strategy.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Structural/Steel Detailing remains core but expanding into Architectural/Interior design post-Edward Farr acquisition; US subsidiaries handle business development/client relations while India centers (Nashik, Latur, Pune) handle execution; Ticket sizes increasing from Rs. 2-3cr to Rs. 8-10cr projects.

business.body: Telge Projects, incorporated in 2018 and headquartered in Pune, provides Structural Steel Design & Detailing, Building Information Modelling, precast engineering, architectural and interior design, construction documentation, estimation and quantity take-off, and project coordination services to clients across the infrastructure, industrial and commercial sectors. It runs a global delivery model combining Indian delivery centres at Pune, Latur and Nashik with offices and subsidiaries across multiple US states, which the Company says enables round-the-clock project execution. A significant portion of business comes from repeat customers and international markets, particularly the United States.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Building Information Modelling (BIM) Solutions:** 3D design validation, clash detection, cost estimation and model-based collaboration, AI-driven BIM tools including predictive data analytics and generative design
- **Structural Engineering Services:** Structural Steel Design & Detailing, structural design and detailing, precast engineering solutions
- **Architectural Services:** architecture and interior design, planning and design coordination
- **Construction Documentation:** 2D drafting, construction documentation
- **Estimation & Quantity Take-Off Services:** material take-off (MTO), quantity take-off and estimation
- **Project Coordination & Engineering Support:** project coordination, integrated project management support

outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Cross-selling architectural services to existing structural clients and vice versa; Geographic expansion into Canada, New Zealand, Southeast Asia; Potential MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) acquisitions to complete full-service AEC offering; AI automation to scale output without linear headcount growth.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Become an integrated end-to-end engineering and BIM solutions provider for the global AEC industry, rather than a niche detailing services vendor.
- Expand geographically across North America, Europe and other high-growth international regions, with named diversification into Canada, New Zealand and Southeast Asia.
- Use value-accretive acquisitions as a core growth lever to add capabilities, client relationships and geographic reach, while maintaining operational integration.
- Scale the newly entered Architecture & Design services segment to create an integrated AEC offering alongside BIM and structural engineering.
- Build specialised engineering capability for the global data centre infrastructure sector.
- Increase participation in industrial, manufacturing, logistics and infrastructure projects.
- Deploy AI, automation and advanced analytics across engineering workflows to improve productivity, quality and project outcomes, including AI-driven BIM tools such as predictive data analytics and generative design.
- Expand BIM-led digital construction and integrated project delivery capabilities.
- Promote environmentally responsible design and sustainable engineering practices aligned with global sustainability objectives.
- Maximise resource efficiency and enhance operational capacity to undertake larger-scale projects (FY27 priority stated by the Chairman & MD).
- Elevate client experience through reliable, cost-effective and technology-driven services, deepening the repeat-client base.
- Retain earnings rather than pay dividend, conserving resources for long-run working capital and business expansion.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Telge Projects is an asset-light engineering services business, so its expansion narrative is footprint, headcount and acquisitions rather than plant capex. During FY26 the Company completed strategic international acquisitions that expanded both its geographic footprint and its service portfolio, strengthening North American market access and taking it into the Architecture and Design services segment — the AOC-1 roster shows Edward Farr Architects, Inc. acquired on 3 March 2026 as a US step-down subsidiary under Telge Global Inc. (formerly Telge Projects Inc.), following Midwest Detailing LLC (January 2024) and Draftco Inc. (December 2024). Operationally the Company reports delivery centres at Pune, Latur and Nashik in India plus offices and subsidiaries across multiple US states, describing '7+ Delivery Centers' in the Corporate Overview; during FY26 it added new delivery centres and enhanced delivery infrastructure, increased overall delivery capacity to support growing client demand, and strengthened engineering capability through strategic hiring. The Company also listed on the BSE SME platform during the year, which the Chairman describes as a catalyst for future growth. The Chairman states that initiatives are underway to expand resources and substantially enhance operational capacity so as to undertake larger-scale projects and enter high-growth, high-demand markets. Investment continues in digital engineering, BIM technologies and process automation, and in an in-house R&D team. Forward capacity intent for FY27-FY30 centres on global expansion across North America and Europe, further value-accretive acquisitions, AI-enabled engineering, and building specialised capability for the data centre infrastructure sector. No rupee quantum, commissioning date, or capacity figure is attached to any of these initiatives anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising global adoption of BIM and digital engineering solutions: management cites the global BIM market growing from USD 9.03 billion in 2025 to USD 15.42 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of 11.3%, driven by urbanisation, infrastructure development, sustainability requirements and digital twin adoption.
- India BIM market momentum from urbanisation, infrastructure investment and government mandates such as the Smart Cities Mission and BIM mandates for public sector projects; India's BIM market projected to expand from USD 350.5 million in 2025 to USD 1.06 billion by 2034 at a CAGR of 11.04%.
- Growth in the global architectural services market, cited at over USD 370 billion in 2025 rising to approximately USD 505 billion by 2031 at a CAGR of around 5.3%.
- US non-residential construction activity remaining supported by infrastructure, institutional and manufacturing investment, with construction real value-added in the United States cited as crossing USD 900 billion during 2025.
- A structural shift in construction spend toward data centres and energy infrastructure, which management expects to be among the fastest-growing commercial construction categories, driven by AI-driven infrastructure demand, grid modernisation and power/digital infrastructure investment — creating incremental demand for structural engineering, detailing and integrated project management.
- Indian infrastructure capex across transportation, metro rail, industrial corridors, warehousing, commercial development and energy infrastructure sustaining demand for structural design and detailing services.
- Digital transformation becoming a competitive differentiator in engineering and construction, with peers adopting BIM, digital twins and AI-assisted project planning — favouring technology-led service providers.
- Rising demand for green buildings, energy-efficient structures and modular construction reshaping project requirements globally.
- Cloud-based BIM deployment expanding real-time collaboration and lowering client upfront infrastructure cost, cited at an expected 55% market share by 2025.
- Asia-Pacific expected to remain one of the fastest-growing architectural services markets globally.
- Repeat-client revenue and long-term customer relationships built on quality, execution accuracy and timely delivery, supporting revenue visibility.
- Margin/productivity lever from integrating digital workflows, advanced design tools and technology-enabled coordination systems to improve execution timelines and resource utilisation.
- The 24-hour execution capability from India-US time-zone complementarity as a turnaround-time advantage in the international engineering services market.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Telge Projects delivered a transformational FY26 with 57% revenue growth driven by the March acquisition of Edward Farr Architects and organic scaling, guiding for 60-70% CAGR while targeting sustained Q4-level margins (35% EBITDA) through higher billing rates ($45-60/hr) and AI integration. The strategic shift from pure detailing to full-lifecycle AEC services significantly expands addressable market and ticket sizes.

one_liner.body: Telge Projects is a Pune-headquartered integrated Building Information Modelling (BIM) and structural engineering services company serving the global Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) industry, with delivery centres in India and an operating presence in the United States.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Telge Projects, incorporated in 2018 and headquartered in Pune, provides Structural Steel Design & Detailing, Building Information Modelling, precast engineering, architectural and interior design, construction documentation, estimation and quantity take-off, and project coordination services to clients across the infrastructure, industrial and commercial sectors. It runs a global delivery model combining Indian delivery centres at Pune, Latur and Nashik with offices and subsidiaries across multiple US states, which the Company says enables round-the-clock project execution. A significant portion of business comes from repeat customers and international markets, particularly the United States.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Telge Global Inc. (formerly known as Telge Projects Inc.) — subsidiary: Direct subsidiary of Telge Projects Limited, incorporated in the USA; acquired 23 December 2023 (the RPT note states subsidiary status with effect from 03 November 2023). Holding vehicle through which the Company holds its US step-down subsidiaries. Reporting period April 1, 2025 to March 31; reporting currency USD.
- Midwest Detailing LLC — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary incorporated in the USA, held 100% by Telge Global Inc.; date since acquired 18 January 2024. Form AOC-1 states 90.86% shareholding, denoting the Company's indirect ownership interest through Telge Global Inc. Reporting currency USD.
- Draftco Inc. — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary incorporated in the USA, held 100% by Telge Global Inc.; date since acquired 27 December 2024. Form AOC-1 states 90.86% shareholding, denoting the Company's indirect ownership interest through Telge Global Inc. Reporting currency USD.
- Edward Farr Architects, Inc. — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary incorporated in the USA, held 100% by Telge Global Inc.; date since acquired 3 March 2026. Architectural practice — consistent with the Corporate Overview statement that the Company entered the Architecture and Design services segment in FY26. Reporting period stated as January to December 31, 2025 (calendar-year reporting, unlike the other subsidiaries). Its % of shareholding cell is blank in the AOC-1 grid supplied. Reporting currency USD.
- Ms. Shraddha Shailesh Telge — related party: Managing Director & CEO; individual owning significant shareholding and/or occupying key management position. RPT note records remuneration payable and unsecured loans taken/repaid.
- Mr. Vishal Uttam Telge — related party: Non-Executive Director; member of the Audit, Nomination & Remuneration and Stakeholders' Relationship Committees.
- Ms. Priti Vishal Telge — related party: Non-Executive Director.
- Mr. Ravi Pandurang Pandit — related party: Independent Director; member of the Audit, Nomination & Remuneration, Stakeholders' Relationship and Risk Management Committees.
- Mr. Avinash Suresh Sachdev — related party: Independent Director; member of the Audit and Nomination & Remuneration Committees.
- Mr. Vinayak Sahebrao Mane — related party: Chief Financial Officer; member of the Risk Management Committee. RPT note records remuneration payable.
- Ms. Barkha Mohit Bharuka — related party: Listed as Company Secretary in the related-party note. Note: the Corporate Information page names Ms. Namrata Vijay Bang as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, suggesting a change in the office during or after the year; the AR text supplied does not state the transition.
- Mr. Shailesh Uttam Telge — related party: Relative of KMP — spouse of Director (Ms. Shraddha Shailesh Telge). RPT note records remuneration payable and unsecured loan repaid.
- Mr. Uttam Telge (Proprietor of Uttam Tools) — related party: Relative of KMP — father of Director Mr. Vishal Telge; proprietor of the entity Uttam Tools.
- Mrs. Shobha Telge — related party: Relative of KMP — mother of Director Mr. Vishal Telge.
- Mr. Suresh Jayraj — related party: Relative of KMP — father of Director Ms. Shraddha Telge.
- Mrs. Maya Suresh Jayraj — related party: Relative of KMP — mother of Director Ms. Shraddha Telge.
- Ms. Akshada Jayraj — related party: Relative of KMP — sister of Director Ms. Shraddha Telge. RPT note records remuneration payable.
- Mr. Shriom Jayraj — related party: Relative of KMP — brother of Director Ms. Shraddha Telge.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Structural/Steel Detailing remains core but expanding into Architectural/Interior design post-Edward Farr acquisition; US subsidiaries handle business development/client relations while India centers (Nashik, Latur, Pune) handle execution; Ticket sizes increasing from Rs. 2-3cr to Rs. 8-10cr projects.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Building Information Modelling (BIM) Solutions:** 3D design validation, clash detection, cost estimation and model-based collaboration, AI-driven BIM tools including predictive data analytics and generative design
- **Structural Engineering Services:** Structural Steel Design & Detailing, structural design and detailing, precast engineering solutions
- **Architectural Services:** architecture and interior design, planning and design coordination
- **Construction Documentation:** 2D drafting, construction documentation
- **Estimation & Quantity Take-Off Services:** material take-off (MTO), quantity take-off and estimation
- **Project Coordination & Engineering Support:** project coordination, integrated project management support

end_markets.body:

- Industrial and manufacturing projects

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Rs. 25cr total active order book (Rs. 10cr from new architectural segment/Edward Farr); 80% sourced from US region; Pipeline: Rs. 6cr in bidding/RFQ stage with 2-4 week conversion window.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: 60-70% CAGR for FY27/FY28; Margins: Targeting Q4 levels sustained (35% EBITDA, 20-23% PAT); Order Inflow: Adding Rs. 4-5cr monthly; Capex/Commissioning: Organic capacity expansion in Nashik/Latur; no major debt-funded capex planned.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Cross-selling architectural services to existing structural clients and vice versa; Geographic expansion into Canada, New Zealand, Southeast Asia; Potential MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) acquisitions to complete full-service AEC offering; AI automation to scale output without linear headcount growth.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rising global adoption of BIM and digital engineering solutions: management cites the global BIM market growing from USD 9.03 billion in 2025 to USD 15.42 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of 11.3%, driven by urbanisation, infrastructure development, sustainability requirements and digital twin adoption.
- India BIM market momentum from urbanisation, infrastructure investment and government mandates such as the Smart Cities Mission and BIM mandates for public sector projects; India's BIM market projected to expand from USD 350.5 million in 2025 to USD 1.06 billion by 2034 at a CAGR of 11.04%.
- Growth in the global architectural services market, cited at over USD 370 billion in 2025 rising to approximately USD 505 billion by 2031 at a CAGR of around 5.3%.
- US non-residential construction activity remaining supported by infrastructure, institutional and manufacturing investment, with construction real value-added in the United States cited as crossing USD 900 billion during 2025.
- A structural shift in construction spend toward data centres and energy infrastructure, which management expects to be among the fastest-growing commercial construction categories, driven by AI-driven infrastructure demand, grid modernisation and power/digital infrastructure investment — creating incremental demand for structural engineering, detailing and integrated project management.
- Indian infrastructure capex across transportation, metro rail, industrial corridors, warehousing, commercial development and energy infrastructure sustaining demand for structural design and detailing services.
- Digital transformation becoming a competitive differentiator in engineering and construction, with peers adopting BIM, digital twins and AI-assisted project planning — favouring technology-led service providers.
- Rising demand for green buildings, energy-efficient structures and modular construction reshaping project requirements globally.
- Cloud-based BIM deployment expanding real-time collaboration and lowering client upfront infrastructure cost, cited at an expected 55% market share by 2025.
- Asia-Pacific expected to remain one of the fastest-growing architectural services markets globally.
- Repeat-client revenue and long-term customer relationships built on quality, execution accuracy and timely delivery, supporting revenue visibility.
- Margin/productivity lever from integrating digital workflows, advanced design tools and technology-enabled coordination systems to improve execution timelines and resource utilisation.
- The 24-hour execution capability from India-US time-zone complementarity as a turnaround-time advantage in the international engineering services market.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 EBITDA margin at 35% driven by higher billing rates ($45-60/hr vs previous $25-35); Employee cost as % of revenue rose to 45% in FY26 due to upfront hiring of leadership/bench strength; Management expects employee cost ratio to stabilize as revenue scales without further leadership hires.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: IPO proceeds utilized for growth capital and acquisition provisions; No debt planned for next 2 years; Equity dilution/rights issue not anticipated in near term; M&A strategy focused on tuck-in acquisitions (like Edward Farr) at ~2.5x EBITDA multiples.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Telge Projects is an asset-light engineering services business, so its expansion narrative is footprint, headcount and acquisitions rather than plant capex. During FY26 the Company completed strategic international acquisitions that expanded both its geographic footprint and its service portfolio, strengthening North American market access and taking it into the Architecture and Design services segment — the AOC-1 roster shows Edward Farr Architects, Inc. acquired on 3 March 2026 as a US step-down subsidiary under Telge Global Inc. (formerly Telge Projects Inc.), following Midwest Detailing LLC (January 2024) and Draftco Inc. (December 2024). Operationally the Company reports delivery centres at Pune, Latur and Nashik in India plus offices and subsidiaries across multiple US states, describing '7+ Delivery Centers' in the Corporate Overview; during FY26 it added new delivery centres and enhanced delivery infrastructure, increased overall delivery capacity to support growing client demand, and strengthened engineering capability through strategic hiring. The Company also listed on the BSE SME platform during the year, which the Chairman describes as a catalyst for future growth. The Chairman states that initiatives are underway to expand resources and substantially enhance operational capacity so as to undertake larger-scale projects and enter high-growth, high-demand markets. Investment continues in digital engineering, BIM technologies and process automation, and in an in-house R&D team. Forward capacity intent for FY27-FY30 centres on global expansion across North America and Europe, further value-accretive acquisitions, AI-enabled engineering, and building specialised capability for the data centre infrastructure sector. No rupee quantum, commissioning date, or capacity figure is attached to any of these initiatives anywhere in this bundle.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident and ambitious; Emphasis on 'transformational' year and global scalability; Transparent about upfront cost investments for future gains; Aggressive on growth guidance (60-70% CAGR) but conservative on debt.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Global delivery model with integrated operations across India and the United States, enabling seamless project execution and client support
- 24-hour project execution capability from time-zone advantage, supporting faster turnaround
- Multi-disciplinary engineering expertise — Structural Engineering, BIM, Precast Engineering, Architecture and Project Coordination delivered under one platform
- Integrated service delivery combining BIM, Structural Engineering and Architectural capabilities for end-to-end project support
- Switching-cost / relationship moat: a significant portion of business is generated from repeat clients, supported by quality, execution accuracy and timely delivery
- Technology-first culture with continuous investment in digital tools, automation and BIM technologies
- Dedicated in-house R&D team driving automation and BIM technology advancement
- Engineering workforce skilled on leading platforms including Tekla, SDS2 and Revit
- ISO 9001:2015 certification supporting consistent quality and compliance
- Industry recognition including Trimble's Feature Company of the Month (2024) and panelist at Tekla User Day (2025)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Receivable days expanded to 108 days (mostly related party, being cleared); Dependence on US market (80% of order book); Potential commoditization of low-end modeling via AI; Execution risk in integrating multiple US acquisitions; Seasonality (Q2 typically slower).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Subsidiaries have zero attrition vs 10% in India; 60-70% of revenue is recurring from existing clients despite project-based nature; Management considers acquired subsidiaries' growth as 'organic' going forward since execution is fully integrated in India; Q4 strength driven by US decision-making cycles.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Become an integrated end-to-end engineering and BIM solutions provider for the global AEC industry, rather than a niche detailing services vendor.
- Expand geographically across North America, Europe and other high-growth international regions, with named diversification into Canada, New Zealand and Southeast Asia.
- Use value-accretive acquisitions as a core growth lever to add capabilities, client relationships and geographic reach, while maintaining operational integration.
- Scale the newly entered Architecture & Design services segment to create an integrated AEC offering alongside BIM and …
